title: 6 Jira Service Management alternatives: How other platforms measure up
summary: Looking beyond Jira Service Management (formerly Jira Service Desk)? Compare alternatives like Zendesk, HubSpot Service Hub, and Freshservice.
body_markdown:
Looking beyond Jira Service Management (formerly Jira Service Desk)? Compare alternatives like Zendesk, HubSpot Service Hub, and Freshservice.


Jira Service Management is a strong choice for IT teams — but[B2B customer support teams](https://front.com/blog/customer-support-operations) often need something different. When customer issues span multiple teams, channels, and systems, a ticket alone doesn’t always provide the context or coordination needed to solve issues efficiently.


That coordination is expensive. Front’s[Coordination Tax report](https://front.com/resources/coordination-tax-report) found that B2B teams spend nearly three hours coordinating for every hour spent solving customer problems. Jira Service Management handles issue tracking and assignment well, but its ITSM, ticket-based model often means switching systems to pull in broader customer context, including prior conversations, account health, and the like.


If the tool isn’t fitting your customer-facing work, weigh these Jira Service Management alternatives against your operating model and desired use case.


## What are Jira Service Management alternatives?


Although Jira Service Management is a popular choice for ITSM and change management, it has limitations for customer-facing work. Here are some aspects teams look for in alternatives:


-


**Connected channels:** The Jira ticket system works well for isolated requests where all the relevant information can be stored in a single ticket. However, customer context may be fragmented across systems, requiring teams to switch between tools.


-


**Clearer ownership:** Jira Service Management offers simple ticket assignment, where one person is responsible for each issue. But B2B support requests often involve coordination among multiple teams, with customer support responsible for communication and engineering owning the bug fix, for example.


-


**Smoother handoffs:** Many B2B customer service teams need more complex automated routing rules,[escalation management](https://front.com/blog/escalation-management) , and workload balancing so that teams can coordinate work and hand off issues without delaying responses.


-


**Better reporting:** In Front’s[Coordination Tax report](https://front.com/resources/coordination-tax-report) , only 5% of B2B companies said they use tools that show them handoff ownership, coordination time, and duplicate work. Some[analytics tools](https://front.com/blog/customer-service-analytics) show how work moves across multiple teams so that you can fix bottlenecks — and that’s not what Jira Service Management is built for.


Put support, operations, product, IT, and account teams on the same request, and the[customer service challenges](https://front.com/blog/customer-service-challenges) pile up fast. When a manufacturing customer reports a defect and stakeholders chase it across different channels, a ticket-per-message model leaves teams duplicating work and contradicting each other.


What works for ITSM won’t necessarily suit[B2B customer service](https://front.com/blog/b2b-customer-service) , and teams may opt for alternatives to Jira Service Management.


## What to look for in a Jira Service Management alternative


IT teams handling technical issues might prioritize help desk software with strong ticket management and ITIL practices. Programs designed for customer-facing teams place more of a focus on clear ownership and the ability to easily collaborate on issues.


### Workflow automation and AI


As customer service teams scale, they can use[automation features](https://front.com/blog/customer-service-automation) like AI-powered triage, routing, escalation, and self-service. These features help you manage growing volumes and complexity by automating routine tasks and freeing up the support team to work on complex customer issues.


The key is to avoid overreliance on automation, given that AI can make mistakes. In Front’s[Coordination Tax report](https://front.com/resources/coordination-tax-report) , more than 70% of B2B companies reported experiencing significant AI-related problems in the past three months. Look for a platform that balances automation with human control when evaluating help desk software.


### Collaboration and visibility


When work crosses support, operations, and other teams, they all need the same real-time view of customer context, ownership, and ticket status. Internal notes and collision detection help too, keeping collaboration clean. For teams coordinating across departments, these are the features that prevent the lost context and unclear ownership that stall responses.


### Scalability, security, and cost


If you’re at a fast-growing company, find a platform that you can adapt as your company acquires more customers and adds more teams and channels. That could mean seeking a wide range of integrations, strong security, role-based access controls, or a pricing model that doesn’t include costly add-ons.


## 6 Jira Service Management alternatives for different service needs


Jira alternatives can range from a similar IT service hub to a platform built for complex collaboration, and the right option depends on your operating model. Here are six platforms, with each one’s strengths and drawbacks.


### 1. Front


[Front](https://front.com/) is a strong choice for B2B service teams seeking a customer operations platform that can help coordinate complex work across multiple teams.


Front’s platform is built around the customer conversation, giving teams a single workspace to manage conversations across different channels. Context, ownership, internal coordination, and follow-up all stay visible in the same customer thread, maintaining clarity as teams manage work.


Front isn’t a direct replacement for Jira Service Management’s ITSM and service desk model. Some B2B teams opt to incorporate both, using Jira Service Management as a structured ITSM tool while relying on Front to coordinate customer-facing conversations across teams.


### 2. ServiceNow


[ServiceNow](https://www.servicenow.com/) is best for large enterprises looking for a powerful cloud IT service hub.


The platform offers extensive workflow automation and an AI-powered self-service portal that can resolve common technical issues. It’s ideal for incident management and IT asset management, with robust analytics and direct integrations with tools like Altiris and Google Maps.


ServiceNow is similar to Jira Service Management, but it’s a more complex system with longer setup and deployment times. It’s a good fit for large organizations but may be overwhelming for smaller ones.


### 3. Freshservice


[Freshservice](https://www.freshworks.com/freshservice/) can complement Freshdesk, allowing companies to connect internal IT support with[customer-facing support](https://front.com/blog/help-desk-solutions) .


The tool offers standard ITSM features like incident management, change management, issue tracking, and problem resolution. It integrates with Freshdesk and more than 1,000 other apps for tasks like collaboration, file sharing, and communication.


Jira Service Management is a better choice than Freshservice for companies that want their IT and development teams to be able to collaborate on issues in the same workflow.


### 4. Zendesk


[Zendesk](https://www.zendesk.com/) is a strong choice for large customer service teams looking for high-volume omnichannel support.


Zendesk’s omnichannel support platform helps teams manage service requests across email, chat, phone, social media, and self-service channels. Its platform and workflows are highly customizable, and it offers AI agents that learn from every interaction.


Compared with Jira Service Management,[Zendesk places](https://front.com/blog/zendesk-alternatives) a stronger emphasis on customer experience and automation, making it a better fit for customer service than IT.


### 5. ManageEngine ServiceDesk Plus


For cost-conscious companies,[ManageEngine ServiceDesk Plus](https://www.manageengine.com/products/service-desk/) is a notable option. At $13 per user per month, its standard plan costs less than Jira’s $20 per user per month.


The platform offers an IT service desk with tools like network monitoring (through integration with a tool like OpManager), incident management, customizable ticket templates, a knowledge base, and a self-service portal. It’s a Zoho product, so it integrates well with other products in the Zoho ecosystem and includes access to the company’s Zia AI agent.


Overall, ManageEngine ServiceDesk Plus offers similar features to Jira Service Management at a lower cost, but may have a steeper learning curve.


### 6. HubSpot Service Hub


[HubSpot Service Hub](https://www.hubspot.com/products/service) can work well for teams that want software tying service work to customer data, sales handoffs, and lifecycle context.


HubSpot’s help desk software smoothly integrates with its popular CRM tool, giving teams access to customer context as they respond to service requests.


Although it isn’t as well-suited to ITSM workflows, HubSpot is a good complement to Jira for teams that want to prioritize consistency across customer relationships.


## Choose Front to manage customer conversations alongside Jira


Even if you enjoy using Jira, you may want to consider adding a different platform for customer-facing work to your workflows. You can use Front for customer conversations, ownership, routing, and follow-up, while your IT team continues to use Jira.


Front’s[Jira integration](https://front.com/integrations/jira) connects customer conversations to Jira work. It lets you create Jira issues directly from Front and bring relevant Jira context back into the customer conversation. This helps you keep customer-facing work coordinated in Front, using Jira for the technical work.
